Tuesday was a tale of two halves in Jaleel's book. The tech and medtech names provided the lift: NVDA added +2.19% and BSX +1.73%, with AZN close behind at +1.77%, enough to keep the session from turning red at the aggregate level. The B of A software price-target sweep gave ADBE a headline tailwind, yet ADBE still finished down –0.85% — a small but pointed reminder that the AI-disruption narrative continues to override improving fundamentals there. NVDA's move came despite a sector-wide semiconductor pullback ahead of tomorrow's Q2 print; the market was clearly positioning, not fading, into earnings.

The drag was concentrated and meaningful. LULU fell –3.62% — Dick's Sporting Goods flagging difficult athletic-apparel conditions adds macro texture to what was already a guidance-cut story with Americas comps running –5% for five straight quarters. That's price and thesis moving in the same bad direction, not divergence — it's confirmation. ONON dropped –2.30% against the same consumer-discretionary headwind, and RKLB shed another –2.01%, deepening an already –14.6% unrealized loss on an AVOID-rated name. EXE also gave back –1.73% with no obvious catalyst beyond a weak energy-sector tape.

The drift to watch is BSX: it's the book's third-largest weight, carries a STRONG BUY verdict and a solid QARP of 74.6, yet management has already guided flat through Q3 after slashing the FY26 growth target from 10.5% to 7–8.5%. Today's bounce is welcome but doesn't resolve that thesis gap. The next data point is October 20 — a long runway for the price to wander. Also keep ADBE on the radar: earnings land September 10, and if the B of A re-rating thesis has legs, that's the confirmation event; if the CFO transition and AI-moat fears resurface, the stock has shown it will punish beat-and-raises.

attention.headline: Q2 earnings drop tomorrow — positioned but exposed
attention.note: At 9.2% weight with an active export-control risk flag and Senate scrutiny, tomorrow's print (Aug 26) is the single largest binary event in the book right now; Jaleel needs a clear stance — hold through, trim into strength, or set a post-earnings trip-wire — before the open.

attention.headline: Dick's macro read hardens the guidance-cut thesis
attention.note: Today's –3.62% move and the Dick's channel check together tighten the bear case ahead of the Sep 2 earnings date; with Americas comps already –5% for five consecutive quarters, the HOLD-QUAL verdict deserves a fresh challenge before that report.

attention.headline: AVOID-rated, –14.6% unrealized, no catalyst visible
attention.note: RKLB is the only AVOID in the book, carries the lowest QARP score at 38.5, and is now down another –2.01% today with no news supporting the position; the case for continued ownership needs to be articulated or the position should be reconsidered.

attention.headline: Thesis drift: STRONG BUY verdict vs. flat-through-Q3 guide
attention.note: BSX bounced +1.73% today but the fundamental gap between a STRONG BUY rating and management's own flat Q3 guidance (after a deep FY growth cut) remains unresolved at the book's third-largest weight, and the next checkpoint isn't until October 20.
